extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for evaluating and articulating obviousness rejections under 35 U.S.C. §103 in light of the Supreme Court's KSR decision; aimed at examiners preparing/recording rejections and factual findings. Emphasizes permissible rationales and required written findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Graham factual inquiries as basis for determining obviousness
rubrics_metrics.description: The factual inquiries in Graham are still the basis for determining obviousness under 35 U.S.C. 103.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners should continue to apply the Graham factors (scope and content of the prior art; differences between the prior art and the claims; level of ordinary skill; and secondary considerations) as the foundational factual analysis when assessing obviousness.

rubrics_metrics.name: TSM test should not be treated as a rigid rule
rubrics_metrics.description: The Supreme Court, in the KSR decision, found that the Federal Circuit’s Teaching, Suggestion, Motivation (TSM) test improperly transformed the general principles of the obviousness analysis into a rigid rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not apply the TSM requirement rigidly as the sole means of establishing obviousness; instead use flexible analysis consistent with KSR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiners must articulate a reason or rationale for obviousness rejections
rubrics_metrics.description: In view of the guidance provided by the Supreme Court in KSR, an examiner must continue to articulate a reason or rationale to support an obviousness rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A rejection under §103 must include a clear explanation of why the prior art would have led one of ordinary skill to the claimed invention—mere conclusory statements are insufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to show TSM does not establish nonobviousness
rubrics_metrics.description: The TSM test can be used as a basis for making an obviousness rejection, but examiners should not conclude that an invention is unobvious simply because a rejection based on TSM cannot be made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Absence of an explicit teaching, suggestion, or motivation in the references is not dispositive; other rationales may establish obviousness under KSR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written record must include findings of fact on teachings and state of the art
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners should ensure that the written record includes findings of fact concerning the teachings of the applied references, and when necessary, the general state of the art to support the obviousness rejection being made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document specific factual findings (what each reference teaches, how the art relates, background/state of the art) so that the rationale for the rejection is supported and reviewable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear articulation of why the claimed invention would have been obvious
rubrics_metrics.description: A key to supporting any rejection under 35 U.S.C. 103 is the clear articulation of the reasons why the claimed invention would have been obvious.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide step-by-step reasoning linking prior art teachings to claim limitations and explain predictability or expectations of success; clarity is essential for defensible rejections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rationale A: Combining prior art elements by known methods yields predictable results
rubrics_metrics.description: Combining prior art elements according to known methods to yield predictable results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the combination of elements is accomplished by established techniques and would produce the expected outcome, that supports an obviousness conclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rationale B: Simple substitution of known elements to obtain predictable results
rubrics_metrics.description: Simple substitution of one known element for another to obtain predictable results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Replacing one known component with another known equivalent that performs the same function in a predictable way can render a claim obvious.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rationale C: Use of known technique to improve similar devices in the same way
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of known technique to improve similar devices in the same way.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applying an established improvement technique to a similar device, producing analogous improvements, supports obviousness if the results are predictable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rationale D: Applying a known technique to a known device ready for improvement
rubrics_metrics.description: Applying a known technique to a known device ready for improvement to yield predictable results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a device is plainly suitable for enhancement and the technique is known to achieve such improvements, obviousness may be found based on predictability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rationale E: 'Obvious to try' when choosing from finite, predictable solutions
rubrics_metrics.description: "Obvious to try" – choosing from a finite number of identified, predictable solutions, with a reasonable expectation of success.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 'obvious to try' only when the number of options is finite and identifiable, the solutions are predictable, and one of ordinary skill would have had a reasonable expectation of success; speculative or unpredictable experimentation is not sufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rationale F: Predictable variations across or within fields based on design incentives
rubrics_metrics.description: Known work in one field of endeavor may prompt variations of it for use in either the same field or a different one based on design incentives or other market forces if the variations are predictable to one of ordinary skill in the art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If market forces or design incentives would lead a skilled artisan to make predictable variations from known work, those variations can support obviousness findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rationale G: The TSM test may still be relied upon as a rationale
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While TSM may be used as one rationale for an obviousness rejection, it should not be treated as the exclusive or rigid test; include supporting factual findings and reasoning consistent with KSR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rationales list is not exhaustive
rubrics_metrics.description: One or more of the rationales set forth in the slides may be relied upon to support a conclusion of obviousness. Note that the list of rationales provided therein is not intended to be an all-inclusive list.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners may rely on other sound rationales consistent with KSR and should ensure each rejection is supported by articulated reasons and factual findings.
